MSA vs Frank-Wolfe Method Comparison

Generated by py-osrm traffic assignment module

Side-by-side convergence and final-state comparison of MSA (α=1/n fixed schedule) and Frank-Wolfe (Beckmann line search) on two TNTP benchmark networks.

Both methods use incremental warm-up, then run up to 20 convergence iterations.

Anaheim

MSA vs Frank-Wolfe convergence comparison on Anaheim (20 max iterations, 100% demand).

Anaheim — TSTT Convergence

MSA final TSTT: 89,878,735. FW final TSTT: 89,826,319.

Anaheim — Wardrop Gap

MSA final gap: 0.007818. FW final gap: 0.005624. MSA uses fixed α=1/n schedule; FW uses Beckmann line search.

Anaheim — State Change Norm

Max absolute change in link flow vector per iteration. Monotonically decreasing by construction for MSA (α=1/n shrinks). FW step size is adaptive and may not shrink monotonically.

Anaheim — Step Size

MSA uses a fixed 1/n schedule (dotted). FW uses Beckmann line search to find the optimal step size each iteration — large early, small near equilibrium.

Anaheim — Final State Comparison

MFD and correlation plots for both methods at their final converged states.

Anaheim — MFD (MSA)

Each point is one link, normalized to per-lane density so links with different lane counts are comparable. Dashed curve: theoretical VDF using median vf=48 km/h, kj=150 veh/km/lane. Left: speed–density. Centre: flow–density (inverted-U fundamental diagram). Right: unserved demand = demand − physical throughput. 337/831 links have unserved demand (total 39,164 veh/hr).

Anaheim — MFD (FW)

Each point is one link, normalized to per-lane density so links with different lane counts are comparable. Dashed curve: theoretical VDF using median vf=48 km/h, kj=150 veh/km/lane. Left: speed–density. Centre: flow–density (inverted-U fundamental diagram). Right: unserved demand = demand − physical throughput. 356/830 links have unserved demand (total 39,114 veh/hr).

Anaheim — Correlation (MSA)

Scatter of per-link flow (left) and travel time (right): our density-based MFD assignment (100% demand, 831 links) vs published BPR equilibrium (100% demand). Dashed line = y = x. Flow ρ = 0.834 (831 matched links). Travel time ρ = 0.710 (831 links).

Anaheim — Correlation (FW)

Scatter of per-link flow (left) and travel time (right): our density-based MFD assignment (100% demand, 830 links) vs published BPR equilibrium (100% demand). Dashed line = y = x. Flow ρ = 0.834 (830 matched links). Travel time ρ = 0.708 (830 links).
